subject: Bare-metal backhaul: asymmetric return path + truncated packets after switch upgrade
messages:
From: Anika Shah <anika@acmecorp.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: frank.liu@edgeworks.io
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent truncated traffic after MX-900 firmware upgrade

Hi Marissa,

We're seeing intermittent application errors for a small subset of sessions across our private backhaul to Redwood's bare‑metal edge after we applied the MX-900 firmware (v3.2.1) last night. Symptoms:
- HTTPS streams to Redwood hosts occasionally drop with repeated TCP retransmits and application-level truncation (partial payloads).
- Affected flows are mostly from our 10.4.0.0/16 → Redwood private CIDR. Return traffic sometimes arrives via an alternate PE and looks truncated.

We captured a short pcap at our egress and attached a slice (pcap-snippet-acme-1.pcap). We also included a traceroute and the switch config diff we applied. Can the Redwood team help validate whether this is an MTU/MSS issue, asymmetric routing, or something on your end (security group/translation)?

Impact: intermittent for 2–3% of sessions; customer-facing API timeouts.

Thanks — we can hop on a quick call if helpful.

—Anika Shah
Network Engineer, AcmeCorp
Anika.Shah@acmecorp.com

Attachments: pcap-snippet-acme-1.pcap, traceroute-output.txt, switch-config-diff.txt

Quick ask for network team: can someone triage path/translation (NAT) + SG rules here? My initial checklist:
- Confirm whether any Redwood edge changed MTU/MSS policies overnight
- Check for asymmetric return paths to Acme's prefixes (BGP adjacencies / route maps)
- Validate NAT behavior (SNAT port exhaustion / conntrack) and any on‑edge MSS clamping

Jonas / Soojin — can you take point? If this is on EdgeWorks PE, loop them in (Frank is on cc). I can coordinate a maintenance window if we need to roll back.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Anika Shah <anika@acmecorp.com>, EdgeWorks NOC <noc@edgeworks.io>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent truncated traffic after MX-900 firmware upgrade

Thanks for the ticket, Marissa + Anika. Quick triage notes from our edge:
1) BGP / routing: I don't see any Redwood-initiated route changes in the timeframe. However, there are intermittent BGP multipath preferences on the PE layer that could cause return traffic to egress via a different POP. I'll attach recent RIB snapshots to the Jira.
2) MTU/MSS: Our edges historically advertise 1500 and expect customer tunnels to negotiate PMTU. The pcap shows TCP segments with MSS ~1460 from Acme, but I can also see retransmits with a likely 1492 fragmentation point (suggesting PPPoE/encapsulation on their side).
3) NAT/conntrack: No global conntrack spikes on Redwood edges, but one of the sessions in the pcap shows a TCP RST with a partial payload — suggests truncation mid-path.

Actionable asks for EdgeWorks/Acme: can you run a controlled traceroute using large probes (1400+ byte UDP/TCP) to each Redwood egress IP so we can confirm MTU drop hops? Also please share the exact switch firmware delta (we have a diff file but need the specific BGP export policies changed).

I'll stand up a tcpdump on the affected edge (edge-nyc2-rd1) and correlate with the timestamps in Acme's pcap. Propose a triage call in 90 minutes to look at captures together.

—Jonas Weber
Senior Network SW Eng, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: Frank Liu <frank.liu@edgeworks.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Anika Shah <anika@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent truncated traffic after MX-900 firmware upgrade

Thanks for the heads up — EdgeWorks NOC here. We reviewed the pcap and switch-config-diff.txt. Preliminary findings:
- We see packet fragments/ICMP fragmentation-needed messages along one of the MPLS legs. That correlates with an MTU mismatch introduced by PPPoE encapsulation on Acme's new MX-900 staging template (interface-level change).
- Also flagged a route-map on PE-13 that prefers a backup path for /24s sourced from 10.4.0.0/16 when a local pref threshold is hit. That creates asymmetric egress for a small percentage of flows.
- We do not see evidence of conntrack exhaustion on our side; no large port reuse or timeouts in the reported window.

Temporary mitigations we can perform immediately (low risk):
1) Enable MSS clamping outbound on PE-13 for the Acme prefix (sets MSS to 1360) — will avoid fragmentation across the MPLS leg.
2) Adjust route-map priority so return path consistency improves for the affected /24s.

If Redwood can confirm MSS clamping or apply an ingress policy on edge-nyc2-rd1 to prefer the primary PE, that should reduce the customer-impacting truncations. We attached a 30s tcpdump slice from PE-13 and a suggested config patch.

—Frank Liu
NOC Lead, EdgeWorks
Frank.Liu@edgeworks.io

Attachments: suggested-pe13-mss-clamp.patch, pe13-tcpdump-snippet.pcap

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Shah <anika@acmecorp.com>, EdgeWorks NOC <noc@edgeworks.io>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bare-metal backhaul: asymmetric return path + truncated packets after switch upgrade

Thanks everybody for the quick triage and the captures — appreciate the thoroughness. Summary and next steps:
- Root cause (likely): combination of Acme's MX-900 PPPoE/encapsulation change + PE-13 route-map preference causing ~2–3% of flows to traverse an MPLS leg with a smaller effective MTU. Fragmentation led to application truncation.
- Immediate mitigations: EdgeWorks to enable MSS clamping on PE-13 (Frank to confirm change applied). Redwood (Jonas) will add a temporary policy on edge-nyc2-rd1 to prefer the primary PE for Acme prefixes until their change is fully validated.
- Medium-term: Acme to revert the interface encapsulation change in staging or work with EdgeWorks to ensure end-to-end PMTU negotiation is preserved; Redwood to add a monitoring alert for inter-POP asymmetric path ratios >0.5%.

I'll create the Jira (NET-4721) and schedule a change window for Thursday 00:30–01:30 UTC to apply and validate the route-map/prioritization steps; Anika, please confirm that time works for Acme.

If the MSS clamping change is applied and we still see truncation, we'll roll back and capture a larger pcap across both edges. Thanks again — looping back after the change window.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
